insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (policy schedule/template shows 'Annual Sum Insured (Rs.)' to be filled; benefit table mentions technological advancements up to ₹1 Crore and worldwide cover max up to ₹3 Crore for Premium plan)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote:
“Reset Benefit Unlimited (Not applicable for unlimited SI)”
“We will reset up to 100% of the Annual Sum Insured, unlimited times in a Policy Year”
great.reference: Policy Schedule benefit table (Base cover #7); Section IV(A)(7) Reset Benefit
great.explanation: Up to 100% of the Annual Sum Insured is restored unlimited times in the same policy year (not applicable if you have an unlimited SI). This can significantly increase available cover if you have multiple hospitalizations in a year.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
great.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

great.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
great.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 180 days after discharge are covered. This supports longer recovery needs like follow-up visits, diagnostics, and medicines.

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote:
“We will provide 20% Loyalty Bonus… at the end of each Policy Year… The Loyalty Bonus will not be accumulated for an amount more than 100% of the Annual Sum Insured…”
“In the event of Claim… the accrued Loyalty Bonus will not be reduced.”
“Loyalty Bonus can only be utilized when the Annual Sum Insured is completely exhausted”
great.reference: Section IV(A)(12) Loyalty Bonus (LB) (also reflected in benefit table #12)
great.explanation: A 20% Loyalty Bonus is added each year up to 100% of Annual Sum Insured and it is not reduced even if you make a claim. The bonus can be used only after the Annual Sum Insured is fully exhausted, which still protects your accumulated buffer.

good.name: Room Rent
good.reference: Policy Schedule benefit table (Base cover #1 In Patient Care)
good.explanation: Any room is allowed except a suite. This gives strong flexibility in room choice without a rupee cap, but suite upgrades will be out of pocket.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.”
good.reference: Section V(A) Pre-existing diseases Code - Excl01
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. Claims for PEDs during this period will be rejected.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.”
good.reference: Section V(B) Specified disease/procedure waiting period Code- Excl02
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are covered only after 24 months of continuous coverage. This delays eligibility for those conditions even if they are not pre-existing.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.reference: Section V(C) 30-day waiting period Code - Excl03
good.explanation: Illness claims are not covered for the first 30 days, while accidents are covered immediately. This mainly affects early claims soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “Additional Base covers in Premium plan 1 Air Ambulance Cover Up to SI”
good.reference: Policy Schedule benefit table (Additional base covers in Premium plan)
good.explanation: Air ambulance is covered up to the Sum Insured under the Premium plan, subject to policy conditions. This can reduce large emergency transport costs if you choose that plan variant.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “We will cover the Medical Expenses incurred in respect of the Domiciliary Hospitalization… provided that: The Domiciliary Hospitalization continues for at least 3, consecutive days”
good.explanation: Home treatment is covered when it qualifies as domiciliary hospitalization and continues for at least 3 consecutive days. This helps when hospital admission is not possible or not advisable.

good.name: PED Waiting Reduction
good.quote: “On payment of additional premium, waiting period… shall be reduced to 24 months…”
good.reference: Section IV(C)(1) Pre-exiting disease (PED) waiting period reduction
good.explanation: By paying an additional premium, the PED waiting period can be reduced to 24 months. This can make the plan more useful sooner if you already have medical history.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote:
“medicines, drugs and consumables (other than those specified in the list of excluded expenses (non-medical) in Annexure I”
(List I includes “GLOVES”, “MASK”, “NEBULISATION KIT”, etc.)
bad.reference: Section IV(A)(1)(e) Inpatient Care; Section VI(B)(12) Non Payables (List I)
bad.explanation: Non-medical consumables listed in Annexure I (e.g., gloves, masks, nebulisation kit) are not payable. This can increase out-of-pocket costs in most hospitalizations.

bad.name: Restore Benefit Restriction
bad.quote: “The Reset Benefit will not be available for an Illness / Injury or related complications including but not limited to any relapse within 45 days in respect of which a claim has been paid in that Policy Year for the same Insured Person.”
bad.explanation: Reset Benefit cannot be used for the same illness/injury (or related complications/relapse) within 45 days of a paid claim in the same policy year. This reduces usefulness for recurring episodes or short-gap readmissions.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote:
“Additional zone based Co-Payment… would be levied on each and every claim in case medically necessary treatment has been taken in a zone higher… than the zone for which premium has been paid”
(Examples shown: “Zone C… Zone A 16%”, “Zone C… Zone B 8%”)
bad.reference: Section VI(B)(1) Zone based premium (zone based co-payment table)
bad.explanation: A zone-based co-pay applies on each and every claim if treatment is taken in a higher zone than the one you paid premium for (e.g., 8% or 16% in the examples). This directly increases your share of every admissible claim in that situation.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: “Cashless treatment is only available at a Network Provider (List of Network Providers is available at our website).”
unclear.reference: Section VII Claims procedure (Cashless Settlement within India)
unclear.explanation: Cashless is available only at network providers, with the list hosted on the insurer’s website. The policy wording does not state the number of network hospitals, so the network size cannot be judged from the document.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
